read.label: Debt costs
read.text: The 10 year Treasury was little changed at 5.07%. Permanent loan rates are priced as a spread over this benchmark, and cap rates tend to follow it over time, so a sustained level above 5% weighs on values and refinancing for loans coming due.

read.label: Floating rate loans
read.text: SOFR was little changed at 3.90%, so the base rate on floating rate loans held roughly flat.

read.label: Renter demand
read.text: The 30 year mortgage rate rose 17 basis points to 7.28%. Rates at this level keep homeownership costly for many renters, which tends to support renewals.

read.label: Vacancy
read.text: The national rental vacancy rate (Census, all rental housing) rose 0.3 points to 7.6% in Q3. Higher vacancy gives renters more leverage, and concessions are typically most common at properties still leasing up.

read.label: Rent inflation
read.text: Rent of primary residence rose 0.2% in October. This measure includes existing leases, so it trails changes in asking rents by several months.

read.label: Phoenix and Seattle
read.text: Phoenix renewal rents are down 2.4%, against a 1.7% gain for the U.S. (Yardi, Sep 2026), consistent with ongoing supply pressure. Seattle apartment vacancy fell to 6.6%, down 0.4 points from a year earlier (Kidder Mathews, Q3 2026).

read.label: What to watch
read.text: Whether the 10 year holds above 5%, the next weekly mortgage rate on Thursday, and the next CPI rent reading.

read_marketing.label: Owner budgets
read_marketing.text: With the 10 year Treasury at 5.07%, owners are paying more for debt, so marketing budgets get a harder look. The plans that hold up show which leases each dollar produced.

read_marketing.label: Renter demand
read_marketing.text: At 7.28%, the 30 year mortgage keeps buying out of reach for many renters. Renewals and referrals carry more weight, so the resident experience is part of the marketing plan.

read_marketing.label: Leasing competition
read_marketing.text: National rental vacancy is 7.6%, so renters have options and compare more communities before they tour. The communities that show up first in Google, Maps and AI answers get the first look.

read_marketing.label: Pricing power
read_marketing.text: Rent of primary residence rose 0.2% in October, a modest pace. When pricing power is limited, reputation, reviews and presentation carry more of the leasing load.

read_marketing.label: What to watch
read_marketing.text: How AI assistants answer apartment questions in your market. Being seen is not the same as being chosen, and that gap can cost tours.
